newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weaker, Dubai sinking, spreads shrink.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaker, Dubai sinking, spreads shrink.

text.p: Asian crude prices were weaker on Monday as confirmation emerged of a weaker MidEast market for March barrels versus February.
Traders said some Japanese traders were looking to sell term barrels of light Middle East grades back into the market as they start to switch their gearing to a spring schedule.
Japanese middle distillate stocks were ample, in the wake of a moderate winter to date, traders said.
Further pressure was coming from weak refinery margins, with no major crudes showing a positive margin. Shell, Esso and SRC in Singapore have all decided to cut runs.
In the swaps market, March/April was quoted at just 20/30 cents and April/May at 30-/40 cents, in as much as 20 cents from Friday.
One trader said there was little indication any Dubai wet cargos had homes to go to, although the Indian Oil Corp tender for March, which closes January 30, might offer some support.
Minas remained reasonably firm after the recent bout of Chinese buying with last deals done at $1.10 by two majors.
Pertamina allocated 90,600 barrels per day of Minas for export in February, from 72,000 in January. --Singapore, N Fullick, (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, K. Takenaka (+813 3432 8837)
